subject: Game Theory
title: Limit Pricing
description: A short lesson to help you apply Limit Pricing.

hook.text: An incumbent sets prices low—not to maximize profit, but to make entry look unprofitable to newcomers.

buildup.text: If the market price is low, potential entrants calculate they can't cover their costs and stay out.

discovery.text: Limit pricing sacrifices some current profit to preserve monopoly power and future earnings.

twist.text: It only works if entrants can't tell whether the low price reflects low cost or strategic intent.

climax.text: Walmart's everyday low prices partly serve this function: new retailers see thin margins and think twice.

punchline.text: Low prices can be a wall, not a gift.

quiz.question: What is the goal of limit pricing?
